output.title: When search is a workflow decision
output.body:
If you are rethinking search in a small business, start with one question: are people repeatedly searching your own business material, or the open web? That difference matters. Repeated searching through customer emails, past invoices, product specs, or help-desk notes is a workflow problem; random web research usually is not.

For an owner-operator, the practical threshold is not “should we use AI?” It is: does this repeated search take a noticeable slice of the week and lead to faster replies, fewer errors, or less back-and-forth? If yes, treat it as one bounded workflow decision, not an AI strategy.

The control is document readiness. A knowledge assistant only makes sense when the useful material already exists in machine-readable form, such as MD, PDF, or structured data. Bareni has a self-built demo that retrieves from approved company documents rather than the open web. It runs locally on synthetic data; the public route is locked. OCR, scan ingestion, rate limiting, and billing are planned, not working.

Keep human approval in place if the output influences customer communication or a business decision. That is Bareni’s policy for high-risk decisions: the system can propose, but the owner decides.

One practical next step is a free 30-minute diagnostic: map one recurring search task, check whether the source material is ready, and decide whether a pilot fits the workflow. If you want numbers, make them joint estimates, not promises.
